Acceptance criteria, test design and UAT

After this lesson you can:
  • Write rule and state-based acceptance criteria
  • Build positive, negative and boundary cases
  • Separate platform verification from tenant UAT

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. Acceptance by rule
  2. Minimum adverse set
  3. UAT and traceability
  4. Regulatory anchors
  5. Where this lives in LoanOS
  6. Knowledge check

1. Acceptance by rule

Use examples and decision tables for eligibility, pricing and authority; transition tables for lifecycle; field contracts for data; and reconciled totals for money. Each expected outcome includes state, reason, evidence and side effects.

2. Minimum adverse set

Test missing/stale evidence, policy boundary, decline/referral, provider timeout, duplicate/replay, tenant leak, unauthorised role, self-approval, revocation, partial settlement, reconciliation break, cancellation, rollback and audit replay.

3. UAT and traceability

Trace obligation and business outcome to requirement, acceptance case, execution evidence and defect. UAT proves configured tenant processes with representative synthetic cases and authorised sign-off; it does not replace security, DR, provider or production-admission evidence.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-IT-GRC — Requirements, change and test evidence must support controlled, auditable processing.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Capability PRD-011 — Golden-case regression.
  • Capability PLT-006 — Synthetic-data sandbox.
  • Capability PLT-009 — Environment promotion.

1. Which case is essential for an approval flow?

  1. Happy path only
  2. Self-approval denial and authority-boundary tests
  3. Colour rendering only
  4. A production borrower
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Segregation and authority failures are core regulated acceptance cases.
